notes: Building and Industrial News, vol. 14 part 1 (Internet Archive buildingindustri1414cont), the 25 weekly issues from 7 January to 24 June 1914. Same method as vol. 14 part 2 of this source and the Building and Engineering News run that follows it: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll year fits, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before the work. The issues were dated from their covers ('Issued Weekly ... Fourteenth Year, No. N', every Wednesday). extract.py ran with BEN_LOOSE=1; the item numbers of the published rows were read from the page image, and unresolved rows whose number was not read carry no extra.item and say so in the locator. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; a cost or name not legible on the image, or past a column or page break, was left out, and where the printed total and the printed instalments disagree no cost is given. Owners who are private individuals are never recorded, nor is a contractor or architect who is the owner, shares the owner's surname, or is listed at the owner's premises; sureties are cut. Held back at the image: storey, unit or use counts that contradict the roll, minor work (small repairs, a brick range, a rear shop), small alterations and plain single houses on parcels with no page (held for a page), entries cut off by a column break, one Oakland address printed under San Francisco, and factory repairs at an address where a later public building stands. One entry printed with a fractional offset ('310-4 13-16 S Cabrillo') was parsed as two lots and merged by hand into the one lot it describes. The contract for fitting up the Forum Club in the Press Club building is recorded on its page without crediting the architect of the fit-up as the building's architect. Three held facts of the Building and Engineering News run (43 Cole Street, 30 April 1921; 530 Sixth Avenue, 24 February 1923; 770 Fourth Avenue, 12 April 1930) were read against their page images and taken up when this volume seeded those pages.

coverage.remaining: Unread: the three earlier half-year volumes on the Internet Archive (vol. 11 pt. 1, 1911, to vol. 12 pt. 1, January to June 1912). In this volume: 148 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; they still need the image check), and 9 more were held for a page at the image. 673 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today. The rest have a nearest parcel that was not accepted.
coverage.note: 2,065 numbered entries read, 1,282 San Francisco rows, 609 placed on a parcel, 139 picked and read against the page image, 98 published on 93 pages (51 seeded; one held fact taken up when the July to December 1913 volume seeded its page), 42 held back at the image.
